definitions.gloss: running for office; standing as a candidate
definitions.explanation: Entering a political election as a candidate. The most common modern use of this word.

definitions.gloss: entering a competition; stepping into the fray
definitions.explanation: More broadly, stepping forward to take on a challenge or competition. Originally referred to riding out to battle on horseback.

notes:
Literally "riding out on horseback" ({出|しゅつ} = go out + {馬|ば} = horse). Originally a military term for riding into battle, now primarily used for political candidacy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{選挙|せんきょ}→選挙：03303_senkyo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{出馬|しゅつば}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to run in an election)
- {出馬|しゅつば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{表明|ひょうめい}→表明：14052_hyoumei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to announce one's candidacy)
- {出馬|しゅつば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見送|みおく}る→見送る：04240_miokuru⟧ (to decide not to run)
- {出馬|しゅつば}⟦{要請|ようせい}→要請：05463_yousei⟧ (request to run for office)

USAGE:
In political contexts, {出馬|しゅつば} is the standard word for announcing or entering a candidacy. The extended sense (a senior person personally stepping in) carries a nuance of someone important entering the scene to take charge.
